n0.speaker: Mum
n0.text: Tobias. Toast. Ninety seconds. And we are talking about last night.
n0.aside: She's got her nurse face on. It is a face for people who are bleeding quietly.

choices.text: "I don't want to carry the lamp, because Wren says it keeps them in."

n1.speaker: Mum
n1.text: You haven't eaten. I can see the cereal box. It's still full.

choices.text: "I ate the cereal that's in my head."

n2.speaker: Mum
n2.aside: The toast pops. Neither of you moves.

n3.speaker: Mum
n3.text: Eat. We'll talk later. You are not in trouble. You're never in trouble. You're just... you.

n4.speaker: Mum
n4.text: Okay. Okay. That's... Okay, sweetheart. Eat your toast.
n4.aside: She says 'okay' four times. That is a record.

choices.text: (Eat. Notice her hand on the kettle: shaking.)

blurt.speaker: Tobi
blurt.text: (You can't hold it in any more.) THE LAMP IS WHAT KEEPS THEM IN AND WREN SAYS IT'S NOT FAIR AND EVERYBODY KNOWS IT AND NOBODY SAYS IT.
blurt.aside: The kitchen goes very still. The kettle clicks off by itself.

end.text: You grab your bag. At the door you wave at the lake. Mum waves too. Her face does the thing grown-ups' faces do when they pretend they're fine.

n0.speaker: Ms. Calloway
n0.text: Tobi, can you tell the class one fact about Little Mercy? Anything you like.
n0.aside: Thirty faces. All of them yours, a little. You've never been this visible.

choices.text: "Fact: we say 'same time tomorrow' because the people in the valley said it to us every night."
"Fact: clocks never change because changing is bad."
"Fact: the Stegosaurus had a brain the size of a lime."

n1.speaker: Ms. Calloway
n1.aside: The room has gone quiet in the way rooms do when the true thing is said at the wrong volume.

n2.speaker: Ms. Calloway
n2.text: That's the town's answer. Thank you, Tobi. Is it yours?

n3.speaker: Ms. Calloway
n3.text: A lime. Wonderful. Class, a lime.

choices.text: (Sit down. Feel your face go hot.)

n4.speaker: Ms. Calloway
n4.text: Come and see me at lunch. Bring your lunch. You're not in trouble. You are, I think, the first person in this room in a very long time to be right.

blurt.speaker: Tobi
blurt.text: (It comes out all at once.) 'CAUSE THEY'RE UNDER THERE, MS. CALLOWAY. THEY'RE ALL UNDER THERE. MY FRIEND WREN IS UNDER THERE.
blurt.aside: Ms. Calloway puts down her chalk, very slowly. The whole room breathes in at once.

choices.text: (Sit down. The class is not breathing.)

end.text: The bell goes. Nobody says goodbye. Everyone waves at the window on the way out, the whole class at once, like a flock of very small, very polite birds.

n0.speaker: Roy
n0.text: Hello, young man. You look like someone I knew.
n0.aside: He is on the porch swing with a Bible in his lap. He is not reading it. It's open at the middle, where the pages have been folded small around something.

n1.speaker: Roy
n1.text: ...A. A boy. Amos. He liked tortoises. You'd have... He'd have... Never mind. Go and play.

choices.text: "Can I see Sir Hours with you tomorrow?"

n2.speaker: Roy
n2.aside: He smells of coal-tar soap and, underneath it, faintly of lake.

choices.text: (Climb up. Let him hold you very tightly.)

n3.speaker: Roy
n3.aside: He unfolds a letter in a child's careful block capitals and, without being asked, puts it in your hand.

n4.speaker: Roy
n4.text: You've got his chin. You know that? He had a great chin. We all said so.

blurt.speaker: Tobi
blurt.text: (You blurt it.) YOU CALLED ME AMOS. YOU'VE CALLED ME AMOS SINCE I WAS FIVE.
blurt.aside: The swing stops. The lake, behind the hedge, makes a sound like someone setting down a cup.

end.text: You wave at the lake from the gate. Behind you, on the porch, Roy waves too. Not at the lake. At you. For a very long time.
